mcqs.question: Under the post-electoral-bond framework, what is not disclosed by an electoral trust?
options: Which company funded which political party
Donor names to the Election Commission
mcqs.explanation: An electoral trust does not disclose which company funded which party. The other details, including donor names, amounts and recipient parties, are disclosed in its annual report to the Election Commission.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Prudent Electoral Trust accounted for ₹33,330.54 crore, constituting 86.38% among the top 10 electoral trusts.
Statement B: In FY 2024–25, it received ₹2,668.49 crore and gave ₹2,180.71 crore to the BJP and ₹216.34 crore to the Congress.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Prudent Electoral Trust accounted for ₹33,330.54 crore and 86.38% among the top 10, while its FY 2024–25 receipts and disbursements were as stated.

mcqs.question: What share of electoral trust funds went to the BJP during FY 2014–FY 2024?
mcqs.explanation: The BJP received 71.67% of electoral trust funds during FY 2014–FY 2024. The figure 84.65% relates to declared direct corporate donations, not electoral trust funds.

mcqs.question: Which institution was the issuer of electoral bonds?
mcqs.explanation: State Bank of India was the issuer of electoral bonds. Prudent Electoral Trust was an electoral trust, not the issuing institution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly lists the denominations of electoral bonds?
mcqs.explanation: The denominations were ₹1,000, ₹10,000, ₹1 lakh, ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore. Each other option omits one denomination from this list.

mcqs.question: What was the validity period of an electoral bond?
options: Until encashment by any political party
mcqs.explanation: An electoral bond was valid for 15 days. The other options do not state the prescribed validity period.

mcqs.question: Which political parties were eligible to receive electoral bonds?
options: Parties securing at least 1% of the votes in the last election
All registered political parties without a vote requirement
Parties securing at least 1% of the votes in the current election
mcqs.explanation: Eligibility required a political party to have obtained at least 1% of the votes in the last election. The current-election condition and the other descriptions were not the stated eligibility rule.

mcqs.question: To which fund were unencashed electoral bonds transferred?
mcqs.explanation: Unencashed electoral bonds were transferred to PMNRF. The Election Commission, the BJP and the Congress were not the specified destination.

mcqs.question: During which period were corporate donations to political parties banned?
mcqs.explanation: Corporate donations were banned during 1969–1985. The other periods refer to different electoral-funding developments and were not the period of the ban.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the legal ceiling on political expenditure?
options: There is no legal cap on party expenditure; only candidates are capped
Both parties and candidates are subject to the same legal cap
Parties are capped but candidates are not capped
There is no legal cap on either party or candidate expenditure
mcqs.explanation: There is no legal cap on party expenditure, whereas candidates are subject to a cap. The other options incorrectly extend or remove the expenditure ceiling.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in relation to parliamentary and legislative privileges.

List-I
(a) Parliamentary privileges
(b) State Legislature privileges
(c) Attorney General
(d) Freedom from arrest in civil cases

List-II
(i) Articles 105 and 122
(ii) Articles 194 and 212
(iii) Privileges extend to this office, but not to the President
(iv) During a session and 40 days before and after it
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. Articles 105 and 122 concern Parliament, Articles 194 and 212 concern State Legislatures, privileges extend to the Attorney General but not the President, and civil arrest protection operates during a session and 40 days before and after it.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Committee of Privileges has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 members in the Rajya Sabha and is semi-judicial.
2. The 2008 Lok Sabha Privileges Committee opposed codification of parliamentary privileges.
3. In State of Kerala v. K. Ajith, privileges were held to override criminal law.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. State of Kerala v. K. Ajith held that privileges do not override criminal law, so statement 3 is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Match the cases in List-I with the corresponding holdings in List-II.

List-I
(a) Pandit M.S.M. Sharma v. Sri Krishna Sinha
(b) P.V. Narasimha Rao
(c) Sita Soren v. Union of India

List-II
(i) Privileges under Article 194(3) prevail over press freedom
(ii) Immunity for bribes linked to speech or vote
(iii) Overruled the JMM bribery case; bribery is not protected
(iv) Privileges do not override criminal law
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii and c-iii. Pandit M.S.M. Sharma concerned Article 194(3) and press freedom, P.V. Narasimha Rao concerned immunity for bribes linked to speech or vote, and Sita Soren overruled that protection for bribery.
